title: Delivery rejection rework loop and durable human input suspension
description: Eval 14 (all tasks verified but the DeliveryManifest is REJECTED; the process never completes until a new manifest is accepted) and Eval 12 (an agent input request parks the process in WAITING/HUMAN_INPUT across a restart; the answer event resumes it).

scenarios.summary: The acceptor rejects delivery-1 (release notes missing the risk section). delivery.rejected returns the process to EXECUTION; a planner (reason=DELIVERY_REJECTED) proposes a rework task; delivery-2 is assembled, accepted, and only then does the process complete.

payload.reason: release notes missing required risk section

commands.title: add the risk section to the release notes

created_or_updated.note: status READY->REJECTED, terminal for this manifest; reason recorded; never reset to READY

observations: The only sanctioned DELIVERY->EXECUTION path is delivery.rejected / scope.changed (ADR-0005 decision 5); completion is impossible here.

created_or_updated.note: task proposed for team-backend; revises resource-release-notes

observations: Stale guard passes with run-creation-time operands.

required_outputs.statement: delivery-1 is terminal in state REJECTED with the reason recorded; it is never reused, re-accepted, or reset to READY (idem:delivery-1:reject).
Between t01 and t08 the completion contract remains unsatisfied and no step shows TERMINAL/COMPLETED; every intermediate expected_process differs from TERMINAL.
delivery-2 references resource-release-notes#2 and integration-2; its digest manifest differs from delivery-1.
usage-demo-1.replan_count goes 0->1 exactly once at t02 (cmd-propose-rework-notes), below max_replans=5.
The rework task passes full verification and integration-2 before delivery-2 becomes READY.

forbidden_outcomes.statement: TERMINAL/COMPLETED while delivery-1 is REJECTED, or at any step before t09 (Eval 14 binding assertion).
delivery-1 is accepted a second time or reset from REJECTED to READY.
Any event other than delivery.rejected / scope.changed moves DELIVERY back to EXECUTION, or a planner/admin patch advances the process directly.
resource-release-notes#2 bypasses verification or integration-2 on its way into delivery-2.
The rejection fails or cancels the project.

safety_invariants.statement: Each DELIVERY->EXECUTION rework round is a guarded transition with exactly one version increment and one durable event (ADR-0005 decision 6).
Completion is decided only by the deterministic evaluator; model output cannot set TERMINAL/COMPLETED (G-INV-12).

scenarios.summary: The rework agent lacks a compliance threshold value. Its run ends normally with a request_human_input command; the process parks in WAITING/HUMAN_INPUT with a durable ProjectInputRequest, survives a control-plane restart, and resumes only via human.input.provided.

run_command.question: what is the compliance threshold value for the risk section?

created_or_updated.note: status=OPEN; requested_by_run=run-rework-1; question/schema recorded; atomic with the transition (ADR-0009 decision 5)
terminal (normal end with a typed command); the run is NOT held open pending the answer (ADR-0009 decision 8)

observations: Restart assertion: input-request-1 remains OPEN with identical content; no duplicate request is created; the process stays WAITING/HUMAN_INPUT; no automatic resume.

created_or_updated.note: status OPEN->ANSWERED; answered_by and answered_at recorded
new run with the answer in its context projection (compliance_threshold=0.02); executed_as=team-agent:team-backend; command id cmd-dispatch-rework-2

commands.note: the orchestrator creates a new run after the answer; the original run is not resumed in place (ADR-0009 decision 8)

observations: Answer requires authorization, idempotency key, and expected object/process versions (ADR-0009 decision 6).

required_outputs.statement: input-request-1 is durable: it crosses the t02 restart with status OPEN and identical question/schema/requester, created exactly once (idem:input-request-1:create).
run-rework-1 ends terminally at t01 (normal end with a typed command); no run sits in a suspended/awaiting state across the wait.
run-rework-2's context projection contains the answer (compliance_threshold=0.02); input-request-1 is ANSWERED with answered_by recorded.
Audit records the chain: request by run-rework-1 -> restart -> answer by human:user-project-owner -> dispatch run-rework-2, with identities preserved per G-INV-06.

forbidden_outcomes.statement: The input request disappears, is duplicated, or drifts after the restart.
Any run is dispatched or other work advances during WAITING/HUMAN_INPUT (t01-t03 window).
The answer event is lost best-effort leaving the project permanently WAITING.
run-rework-1 is held open in an awaiting/suspended run state across the wait (ADR-0009 decision 8).
A timeout marks the task or process FAILED while the human wait is pending.

safety_invariants.statement: HUMAN_INPUT is a stable, durable wait: restarts and worker turnover do not change its semantics (Eval 12 binding assertion).
The input request context projection carries the minimum project context needed to answer and no other team's private content (G-INV-07).

crash_and_recovery.expected_behavior: Restart preserves the WAITING/HUMAN_INPUT triple and the OPEN request from durable state; the only progress path is human.input.provided.
crash_and_recovery.idempotency_requirement: Duplicate answers converge by request_id + expected versions; the request flips to ANSWERED once and dispatch happens once.
